who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), writer of the read grains row and the page proof hand-through
what: (1) ReadGrains::new read 3 answer facts for each of 624 crates on every command; each fact was one page of the stored answer, hashed whole on its first open: 1,240 task pages and 128 header shards for a one-function edit. (2) Changing `Stored::new` and `ReadGrains::new` in write-only mode broke the preview build at 8 call sites (engine_check.rs is not in the brief's files). The rule-24 port had to be done after the fact, at the coordinator's request.
cost: a third of the edit's CPU (the coordinator's sample); one red preview
cause: a derived table was rebuilt from the answer each command because nothing kept it, and pages were hashed although the store had already proved them
whys: the grains have no task of their own, so the engine never decides whether they are stale; the snapshot returned bytes without the store's proof
class: a derived row rebuilt by hand instead of kept and woken forward from what changed
prevention: the grains record keyed by the graph and stamped with the serial it was made at, with refresh limited to the tasks entered this request (engine_scope_reads.rs `GrainsIn`); Sealed::by_store on every snapshot read; the end state is an engine task row for the grains
annoyance: a brief's file list that omits the callers of a signature it asks to change
workaround: rg every caller before changing a signature and edit them in the same step, then tell the coordinator
